bugs_found: compound_interest: division r/n uses integer n without Decimal conversion in some Python contexts is fine but mixing precision; also missing validation that principal can be negative (allows negative principal silently)
loan_payment: when r == 0 returns p/m as Decimal/int division which works but inconsistent with other branch returning Decimal; no upper bound on months allowing DoS via huge exponentiation

transfer: non-atomic mutation - if exception occurs between debit and credit, account_from is already debited (partial state); the post-debit check 'if balance < 0' is dead code since insufficient balance is checked before
transfer: amount is not converted to Decimal, so passing float/int mixed with Decimal balance can raise TypeError or cause precision issues
apply_fee: fee computed as a*pct treats pct as a fraction but no validation that pct <= 1 (e.g. pct=2 means 200% fee, returning negative result)
apply_fee: can return negative value when fmin > a (minimum fee exceeds amount)
fx_convert: no validation that rate is positive; negative or zero rates accepted silently
fx_convert: rates dict lookup is one-directional - no fallback to inverse rate (to,from) -> 1/rate
General: no logging/audit trail for financial operations
General: Decimal context/precision not explicitly set, relying on default which may cause rounding inconsistencies across environments
General: no thread-safety on transfer mutating shared Account state
